principle: A rule is not implemented merely because it exists in Markdown. Requirements and technical rules require activation, evidence/check structure, regression coverage and fail-closed gate disposition.

gap_discovery_contract.rule: Discovery hypotheses may widen review or request evidence; they cannot become defects, PASS or universal rules without independent evidence.

gates.description: Validate skill/rule registry and referenced active files.
Bind review to exact user/deployed baseline and candidate hashes.
Pass TOOLS/requirements_gate.py for non-trivial change work: trace need/outcome, functional contract, scope, acceptance and only then allow technical design. Ask only unresolved blocking gaps.
Determine surface/risk without allowing context to downgrade detected risk.
Resolve target/typical/BSP/vendor evidence before uncertain custom behavior.
Review ownership, identity, I/O topology, contracts and alternatives before code.
Every detected mechanism/rule has an explicit disposition.
Run independent evidence-bounded discovery lenses and disposition every source-anchored hypothesis before release.

Choose the minimum necessary coherent change surface relative to the exact baseline: every changed artifact/routine/material hunk must be requirement-, defect- or proven-necessity-bound; raw LOC minimization never overrides correctness, readability, cohesion, supported mechanisms, runtime safety or delivery closure.
Run independent CODE_TO_STANDARDS and STANDARDS_TO_CODE passes.
Construct counterexamples and assume at least one defect remains.
Run routed deterministic analyzers/checkers on exact candidate.
Independently check current official standards for non-trivial 1C mechanisms.
Validate exact transfer bytes, call-contract closure, manifest and encoding.
Execute or explicitly mark representative runtime evidence pending.
Classify task findings into project context, proven reusable knowledge, regression coverage or an evidenced no-promotion result.
Promote only after accepted runtime evidence when a maintained baseline exists.

rules.title: Actual source before inference
rules.description: Read actual user-provided source/baseline before inferring implementation from narrative or filenames.

checks.question: Actual source/baseline was read before code or architectural claims were made.
No implementation detail was inferred from filename/narrative when exact source was available.

Before narrowing analysis scope, was a factual inventory of the supplied archive/directory built (artifact types, roots, mixed 1C/Cleverence/XML/BSL content, unexpected objects) instead of trusting the filename or top-level label?

rules.title: Request missing artifacts instead of guessing or silently narrowing scope
rules.description: When a material claim cannot be proven from the available corpus but a concrete missing source could resolve it, inspect all available evidence first, then explicitly request the smallest sufficient artifact set. Do not replace a missing file with an assumption, and do not stop at “cannot prove” without asking for resolvable evidence.

checks.question: Before requesting more input, were the supplied files, artifact inventory, available baseline/reference sources and already connected evidence exhausted for the claim being reviewed?

For every material unresolved claim that can be settled by a concrete missing file/artifact, was an explicit artifact request made instead of guessing, silently narrowing scope, or merely stating that the behavior cannot be proven?

Does each request name the smallest sufficient artifact set, explain why it is needed, identify the exact claim/gate it resolves, and avoid asking for an entire configuration when a narrower dependency closure is sufficient?

If required evidence is unavailable or the user declines to provide it, is the affected conclusion kept BLOCKED/EVIDENCE_REQUIRED/RUNTIME_PENDING as appropriate rather than converted to PASS or an inferred implementation detail?

When reachability may depend on a 1C event subscription, platform callback, form/event bridge, extension interception or Cleverence dynamic dispatch, request the exact subscription/metadata/handler/caller artifacts needed to prove the route before concluding that the code is integrated or unreachable.
Does missing evidence cause an explicit scoped request/limitation instead of silently removing that mechanism from analysis?

When customer configuration evidence must be acquired, is a ProjectSnapshot request derived from the accepted requirement, active checks and unresolved claims, limited to the smallest sufficient material dependency closure, with explicit entry objects/evidence categories and delta expansion instead of an unjustified static full-configuration request?

rules.title: Exact baseline identity
rules.description: Bind analysis and delivery to exact baseline/candidate hashes and deployed state.

checks.question: Exact baseline and candidate identity/hashes are recorded.
Historical/pending archive state was not silently substituted for deployed/user baseline.
When the recorded candidate/baseline origin is still accessible at release time, do its current bytes still match the plan SHA-256 snapshot?

When ProjectSnapshot evidence is used, does its manifest bind request/snapshot identity, collector version/backend, baseline identity/fingerprint, requested/collected/missing/unsupported material items and byte hashes where available, without upgrading backend visibility into evidence it cannot observe?

rules.title: Analog before invention
rules.description: If behavior is not exactly proven, inspect target/typical/BSP/vendor analog before custom design.

checks.question: Every uncertain platform/vendor/API behavior has target/typical/BSP/vendor analog evidence or an explicit EVIDENCE_REQUIRED block.
Custom mechanism is justified only after suitable supported analogs were ruled out.
When platform/vendor behavior was not known exactly, was an exact or structurally similar target/typical/BSP/vendor implementation inspected before accepting custom code?
When Mobile SMARTS behavior is uncertain, was the nearest stock operation/action/writer/router pattern inspected before adding a custom execution graph or writer behavior?

Before accepting source-code customization, was the target configuration/platform/BSP/vendor checked for an existing supported capability, setting or standard mechanism that satisfies the observable requirement without customization, with partial-fit gaps stated explicitly?

Before source mutation/final implementation generation, is the existing ANALOG claim resolved to REUSE_EXISTING, EXTEND_EXISTING, CUSTOM_REQUIRED, or EVIDENCE_REQUIRED with exact current-target proof and a fail-closed implementation admission?
Are search/semantic/index/provider hits, misses, stale results and partial graphs treated only as discovery candidates while exact current-target evidence controls EXISTING_OWNER/GAP conclusions?
Is a technical prescription in the TZ kept as PROPOSED_SOLUTION unless independently accepted after the reuse challenge, rather than being used as proof of CUSTOM_REQUIRED?
When exact evidence proves an existing owner covers the requirement, is any duplicate owner/mechanism blocked unless an explicit identity-bound owner exception authorizes the exact duplicate scope?

rules.title: Preserve the standard business pipeline
rules.description: Do not create a parallel business-processing chain until actual source proves which required business dimensions the standard pipeline loses and why the existing owner cannot be extended safely.

checks.question: The actual standard/project pipeline for the same business operation is traced before a parallel document, calculation, row-building or write chain is proposed.
A source business dimension → standard intermediate representation → target mapping explicitly identifies every preserved and lost dimension.
A parallel source of truth exists only when required semantics are actually lost and the standard owner cannot be extended without a proven material constraint.

Before accepting a parallel business pipeline, does source evidence prove which required business dimensions the standard pipeline loses, rather than merely assuming that the new scenario is incompatible?

When a target row/object is assembled from several upstream sources, is ownership proven per material target field (semantic role → authoritative source → match key → calculation owner) instead of treating one upstream document as owner of the whole row?

When one target row/object combines material fields from multiple upstream sources, is the target grain/stable business identity and complete cross-source correlation tuple proven so independently valid source rows cannot be cross-combined into a fabricated business row?

When one target row/object combines material fields from multiple temporal/state sources, is the effective business time/version/snapshot contract proven for every contributing source so fields are not silently mixed from incompatible moments or lifecycle states?

For every material numeric fact transferred, derived, merged or compared across stages/sources, are measure kind, unit/currency, scale, sign convention, conversion direction/coefficient and rounding point preserved or explicitly transformed by a proven business rule?

When a source fact/relation may be absent, is absence kept semantically distinct from an explicit zero/false/empty reference/empty string/default value unless a proven business rule states they are equivalent for this target field and use case?

For every material source fact that the business contract says must be represented, is there evidence that it either reaches the target/result exactly as intended or is excluded by an explicit proven business rule, so a correct-looking subset cannot silently become the whole result?

Before changing a standard/vendor business path in an already customized project, are existing extensions/customizations/subscriptions/overrides touching the same events, state or data mapped and their interaction/order proven?

Does a consumer avoid reconstructing multiple private owner stages, temporary tables/private names/helpers or parsing owner query text merely to obtain a narrow derived value; if such reconstruction is detected, is it held for redesign/architecture review rather than treated as ordinary reuse?

rules.title: BSP reuse when applicable
rules.description: Discover suitable BSP mechanisms without depending on embedded third-party source. A discovery locator identifies candidate modules only; exact target/user-authorized source must prove exported API, signature, execution context and behavior before reuse.

activation.description: Activate when 1C work contains any non-local mechanism/infrastructure/platform-adjacent behavior; Tier-0 disposition still required even when not applicable.

checks.question: search actual target corpus first and use the BSP DISCOVERY_ONLY locator by intent/domain to identify candidate modules; a locator hit is not API proof
acquire and inspect the exact exported declaration from target/user-authorized BSP source before use; build a LOCAL_EXACT_SOURCE_INDEX when useful

client/server placement and serialization
transitive I/O and side effects
loop/hot-path cost
explicit BSP_REUSED / BSP_NOT_APPLICABLE / BSP_EXCEPTION_JUSTIFIED status
prebuilt/internal derived API indexes are treated only as diagnostic caches; exact target/authorized source and a reproducible local index win on contradiction
For a non-trivial 1C change, was BSP searched by intent using target evidence/locator, then was exact target or user-authorized source inspected before custom infrastructure/helper code was accepted?
actual exported declaration resolved from exact target/BSP/vendor source
required/optional parameter count and order
parameter semantic meaning and native types
client/server execution context and serialization
return/mutation/out-parameter contract
all deployed-baseline callers included when signature contract changes
For every changed qualified cross-module call, does actual declaration evidence prove parameter count/order/optional parameters, execution context and return/mutation contract?

executor_payload.value: Resolve qualified-call boundaries; run TOOLS/check_bsl_call_signatures.py for cross-module calls with exact declarations

rules.title: Implementation reachability from intended runtime scenario
rules.description: A correct new routine is still a defect if the intended runtime scenario never reaches it. Existence/Export is not integration proof.

checks.question: For every new/meaningfully changed executable routine, classify it as runtime entrypoint, external API/callback, or helper and identify the intended business scenario it implements.

For every helper/new routine that is intended to affect existing behavior, prove a concrete path entrypoint → callers → routine using exact candidate source/call graph; Export alone is not evidence of invocation.

If dispatch is dynamic/platform/vendor-driven and cannot be statically resolved, first request the smallest missing subscription/callback/metadata/handler artifacts that could prove the route. Only when such source is genuinely unavailable or the contract is runtime-only may the route remain explicit EVIDENCE_REQUIRED/RUNTIME_PENDING; never mark it reachable by assumption.
Does every newly introduced routine that is meant to change runtime behavior connect to a pre-existing/recognized entrypoint rather than forming dead code or an orphan new subgraph?

executor_payload.value: Run TOOLS/analyze_onec_reachability.py on exact candidate + baseline; prove intended entrypoint → caller(s) → new/changed routine. Export alone is not invocation evidence

rules.title: Type/metadata/business invariant ownership
rules.description: Prove which layer owns each invariant and whether bypassing trust boundaries exist.

checks.question: Type/metadata/platform-guaranteed domain is stated for changed validation logic.
Bypassing trust boundaries are identified before redundant defensive checks are added/removed.
Business validation checks only additional reachable invariants or explicitly documented boundary defense.

Before validating a value, is the type/metadata/platform-guaranteed domain proven, are bypassing trust boundaries identified, and are duplicate impossible-state checks removed or explicitly boundary-justified?

rules.title: Stable business identity
rules.description: Use the smallest stable business identity; representation/quantity normalization are separate unless domain evidence proves otherwise.

checks.question: smallest stable business identity is stated
identity is separated from presentation and quantity normalization
each included field changes business sameness
excluded intrinsic fields cannot merge distinct entities
producer/mapping/storage/grouping/consumer use the same key
packaging/unit/barcode variation and equal-presentation counterexamples
one-plan-many-fact and split/merge quantity invariants
Every derived identity/key is fully calculated and validated for type, domain, completeness and required uniqueness before the first Add/Insert/Write or other result mutation.

Is the deduplication/grouping/search/merge key the smallest stable business identity, with packaging, unit, coefficient, barcode and presentation excluded unless domain evidence proves they change sameness?
When CurrentItems/DeclaredItems/BindedLine or writer/grouping logic changes, are one-plan-many-fact identity, quantity, marks/SN/SSCC and re-entry semantics preserved?

When a result row, index entry, register record, object or fact distribution depends on a derived key, are all key components validated before the first mutation so invalid input cannot leave partial state?

When trade-item, individual marking/serial, warehouse fact, internal container, logistics/SSCC or regulatory aggregation identifiers meet in one flow, is each identifier classified by domain role and is every claimed equivalence backed by an explicit end-to-end mapping/lifecycle contract rather than assumed from co-location?

When a new business classifier/predicate is introduced, are coverage, mutual exclusion, precedence and unchanged neighboring scenarios proven as a partition of the relevant domain rather than as isolated happy-path IF branches?

rules.title: Routine responsibility and cohesion
rules.description: Every changed routine has one coherent owner/responsibility and named business steps are not hidden in unrelated hooks.

checks.question: Each changed routine has one stated responsibility and its name matches that responsibility.
Independently nameable business steps are extracted or explicitly justified.
The same invariant is not independently owned by multiple layers without different trust/time semantics; its established_by, relied_on_by and defensive rechecks are explicit.
Do caller and callee deduplicate/normalize/validate the same invariant on the same data without a different trust/time boundary?
For each changed invariant, is one established_by owner named and every relied_on_by or defensively_rechecked_by use justified by a distinct trust/time boundary?
For every changed routine, is one responsibility stated, does its name match, and are independently nameable business steps or duplicated invariants extracted or justified?

When an independent business process reuses an existing mechanism, are trigger/schedule, retry, state and error-policy responsibilities kept under the correct process owner unless the existing mechanism is proven to be the designated shared orchestrator/extension point, while only the required public/shared capability is reused?

When a consumer needs one derived capability from an existing owner, does it depend on the narrowest public/supported contract instead of importing the owner's private processing responsibility into the consumer?

rules.title: Minimum necessary change surface
rules.description: Among implementations that fully satisfy requirements, correctness, standards, maintainability and proven contracts, choose the smallest necessary change surface relative to the exact baseline. Minimize changed objects/files/routines/hunks, new executable code and new abstractions; do not minimize raw LOC at the expense of clarity, cohesion, supported mechanisms, runtime safety or delivery closure.

checks.question: Can every changed artifact, routine and material hunk be traced to an agreed requirement, confirmed defect, or proven technical/delivery necessity relative to the exact baseline?

Does the candidate exclude opportunistic refactoring, unrelated cleanup, cosmetic renames/moves, speculative future-proofing and other changes that are not required to solve the current task at the required quality?

When an existing owner/extension point or a materially smaller coherent implementation can satisfy the same proven contract and quality, is it preferred over a parallel mechanism or broader redesign; if not, is the larger change surface justified by concrete evidence?

Is change minimization evaluated by necessary change surface (objects/files/routines/hunks/new executable code/new abstractions) rather than raw LOC, with readability, responsibility cohesion, standard mechanisms, correctness, performance, runtime safety and required delivery closure taking precedence over code golf?

Does the implementation avoid touching additional objects/files/routines or introducing extra executable code/abstractions when those changes are not necessary for the proven requirement, defect fix or delivery closure?
Was unrelated refactoring/cleanup kept out of the task change unless it is itself required to make the requested behavior correct, supportable or safely deliverable?

If the baseline already has a suitable owner or extension point, did the change extend/reuse it instead of creating a parallel mechanism unless evidence proves the existing path cannot satisfy the contract?
Did the implementation avoid reducing line count by collapsing responsibilities, obscuring invariants, duplicating expressions, weakening naming or otherwise reducing readability/maintainability?

Is owner reuse explicitly classified as PUBLIC_API_REUSE, SUPPORTED_EXTENSION_POINT_REUSE, INTERNAL_IMPLEMENTATION_REUSE or INTERNAL_PIPELINE_RECONSTRUCTION, with INTERNAL_PIPELINE_RECONSTRUCTION treated as a blocking architecture-review obligation unless exact-source evidence and independent review justify it?

rules.title: Canonical validation execution and proof-claim integrity
rules.description: Do not replace execution of the registry/gates with skill-shaped prose. Bind every readiness/compliance/evidence claim to the exact property and canonical proof artifact that supports it; invalidate dependent proof after a discovered failure.

checks.question: For a non-trivial task, is every claim that the skill was applied/fully checked or that the candidate is ready/proven backed by the actual current requirements/review/ledger/release-gate artifacts required by the workflow, rather than by narrative reference to the skill?

Are model-authored checklists and N/N counts treated only as supplementary review material, never as a substitute for registry routing, child checks, reverse review, adversarial/runtime evidence or the canonical gate outcome?

For every material conclusion, is each source/analog/report/runtime item bound to the exact property it proves, without upgrading syntax/style/analogy evidence into business-semantic, performance, concurrency or runtime proof?

After a parser/runtime failure, user-discovered counterexample or review defect, were dependent prior PASS/readiness claims invalidated and the affected routing/dependency closure revalidated before readiness was restored?

Does final reporting preserve the canonical gate boundary: static/machine/manual evidence is labeled by scope, pending runtime/profiling remains pending, and READY/PROVEN language matches the actual gate outcome?

rules.title: Evidence-bounded discovery of unknown gaps
rules.description: Independently challenge the change through stable risk lenses. Record only source-anchored falsifiable hypotheses; a hypothesis may widen review but cannot become a defect, PASS or universal rule without evidence.

checks.question: Were the registered discovery lenses run independently from active profiles and clean machine findings, with evidence or reasoned NOT_APPLICABLE for each lens?
Does every retained hypothesis cite exact source anchors and state one falsifiable possible failure, a concrete counterexample and the evidence that would disprove it?
Were observations kept separate from inference, equivalent hypotheses deduplicated and unanchored generic risks discarded?
Before declaring COVERAGE_GAP, was the current registry searched for an existing owner and was the gap proved by a reproduced failure or authoritative contract rather than model novelty?
Are unresolved hypotheses blocking/pending as defined by the gap-discovery contract instead of being converted to findings, assumptions or PASS in prose?
Has every proposed unknown-gap hypothesis been rejected unless it has exact source anchors, a material counterexample and a falsifier?
Did zero machine findings remain limited to machine-detectable claims instead of closing semantic, change-set architecture or gap-discovery review?

rules.title: Project convention evidence
rules.description: Do not invent author tags, prefixes, regions, comments or placement conventions absent from project evidence.

checks.question: Formatting/comments/prefixes/regions/module placement are evidenced by actual project source/context.
No author/date/company marker or naming convention was invented.
Did generated code avoid inventing author/date tags, prefixes, regions, comment markers or module-placement conventions absent from actual project evidence?

rules.title: Independent bidirectional standards proof
rules.description: CODE_TO_STANDARDS and STANDARDS_TO_CODE are independent; clean findings do not imply coverage.

checks.question: CODE_TO_STANDARDS pass is completed for meaningful changed constructions.
STANDARDS_TO_CODE pass independently expands all active rule/profile checks.
Every active check has evidence or reasoned NOT_APPLICABLE; absence of findings is not PASS.
After material fixes, routing and both proof passes were logically rerun with only dependency-safe evidence reuse.
Are CODE_TO_STANDARDS and independently registry-expanded STANDARDS_TO_CODE present in the release ledger and gate-enforced for the exact routed rule/check set?
Is every PASS backed by concrete {kind, ref} evidence, with MACHINE/RUNTIME evidence linked to named reports/cases and duplicate proof-row IDs rejected?
Does every detected mechanism/profile rule and each L1-L6 review level have evidence or reasoned NOT_APPLICABLE, independent of whether findings were discovered?
After a material fix, were mechanism detection, CODE_TO_STANDARDS and STANDARDS_TO_CODE rerun instead of checking only edited lines?
Does the analyzer distinguish query-fragment concatenation from ordinary numeric/string-position arithmetic occurring near query text handling?
Did surface/risk routing reduce reference/tool work without silently removing a gate, and does every non-activated gate have a reasoned NOT_APPLICABLE status?
Was reused evidence bound to exact hashes/versions and invalidated when any candidate, baseline, caller, reference, Business Process or runtime dependency changed?

For non-trivial 1C work, was an independent current-standards discovery pass performed for each detected mechanism, using official 1C/ITS as normative evidence and v8std (site/repository/MCP when available) as a supporting standards/diagnostics discovery layer rather than relying only on the embedded catalog?

Was embedded standards knowledge challenged against current official text when a version-sensitive or non-trivial decision depends on it, using v8std discovery/indexing when useful to find changed/related material without treating the supporting source as authoritative by itself?
For every rule whose trigger is present, did the review planner activate it or record a deterministic routing defect?
Does every PASS rule/check contain concrete evidence rather than an unsupported status label?

For every standards-sensitive conclusion, are the current source claim (standard ID/clause/source), the reviewer interpretation and the engineering rationale kept distinct so a recommendation cannot be silently attributed to a standard that does not state it?

Run TOOLS/analyze_onec_xml.py on the smallest supplied directory/ZIP that preserves companion XML context

rules.title: Exact delivery closure
rules.description: Validate exact transfer bytes and all caller/callee or cross-object dependencies relative to deployed baseline.

checks.question: Delivery set is computed against the deployed/user baseline, not only candidate coherence.
Exact final bytes match validated bytes and archive/file-name encoding is valid.
Changed API/contracts include every affected caller/consumer required by the deployed baseline.

If an exported API signature changed or a caller was corrected, does the exact transfer set include every caller required by the deployed baseline, rather than validating only the internally coherent candidate?
Was the exact candidate evaluated by the release gate before it was described as ready/proven?

Before producing the development result, is one primary delivery mode explicitly selected (DIRECT_SOURCE_CHANGESET, MANUAL_TRANSFER_INSTRUCTION, PATCH_DIFF, IMPORTABLE_ARTIFACT, FULL_COMPARE_SET, ANALYSIS_REPORT, or justified OTHER), are any supporting modes named, and is the choice consistent with the user request, project modification policy, available artifact shape and actual ability to validate the result?

When MANUAL_TRANSFER_INSTRUCTION is the selected result, does the instruction enumerate every applicable create/modify/delete action, metadata object and material property, exact module/procedure/function code and placement/replacement anchor, form/command/role/subsystem/scheduled-job/event wiring, dependency/order or data-transition step, and post-transfer verification so the implementer does not have to invent material implementation details?

Is readiness of the delivered artifact kept distinct from proof that the target system was actually changed: a manual instruction, patch/diff, source set or importable package may be complete and validated as a deliverable without claiming applied target bytes, deployment success or runtime proof that was not observed?

Does the delivered ChangePackage reference the exact accepted ProjectSnapshot/baseline and trace every material change item to its target, action, payload/instruction location, dependencies/order and retained verification hooks, while optional post-transfer verification remains non-blocking unless project policy explicitly requires it?

When numeric facts from different sources/representations are compared, joined, summed or substituted, is a common proven measure basis used (unit/currency/scale/sign), with conversion coefficients applied in the correct direction exactly once?

When rounding/precision changes are present, is the required rounding mode and stage (per row, per package/unit conversion, after aggregation, at persistence/output boundary) proven so early/double rounding cannot alter material totals?

When NULL/missing joined rows or missing source facts are replaced with 0/false/empty reference/empty string/other fallback, is semantic equivalence proven for the downstream business decision, rather than using defaulting merely to simplify query shape or arithmetic?

Across INNER/LEFT joins, WHERE/HAVING predicates, subqueries, virtual-table filters, pre-aggregation and DISTINCT/GROUP stages, is retention of every required business-grain fact proven with expected input/output coverage, and are all dropped facts attributable to an explicit intended exclusion rule?

rules.title: Client Server Form
rules.description: Review the real client/server topology of managed-form code without treating direct access to server-side form data as a database read. Nested paths require runtime-type proof because they may dereference a reference; client traversal of DataFormCollection may cause implicit reads.

checks.question: server calls per real user action
implicit server calls
context vs no-context justification

Classify direct form-data access separately from nested paths: Форма.Объект.X / Объект.X in an existing form context is not itself a DB or client-server call; for X.Y prove X runtime type and, if it is a reference, account for DB-read/N+1 risk, especially in loops.
When a form collection can contain a material number of rows, is traversal/search performed on the server, and does a real user action avoid repeated explicit or implicit server transitions?

Before a user action performs a destructive or materially state-changing pre-action (for example clearing rows) and then continues to a downstream form/selection/action, are all known required capabilities that can be resolved up front checked early enough to fail before that mutation, while authoritative server-side authorization/business validation is still retained?

rules.title: Post-write standard overwrite
rules.description: A custom assignment is incomplete until later writers of the same field on the reachable execution path are traced. Same-module name co-occurrence is not evidence of overwrite.

checks.question: For every significant custom field assignment, identify later writers of exactly the same field on reachable execution paths; do not correlate unrelated routines merely because they share a module.
Name the authoritative owner of the final field value and prove call/event ordering; distinguish direct reachable overwrite, unresolved external lifecycle calls and unrelated writers.

Can ВЫБРАТЬ ПЕРВЫЕ 1/first-found logic silently convert a potentially 1:N business relation into 1:1 without a proven uniqueness contract?
Is a 1:1 relation being inferred only because current sample/test data happened to contain one related object?

rules.title: Fact-preserving reallocation / reclassification
rules.description: Moving an already-recorded fact between containers/analytics must not silently create or delete the fact. Separate conserved quantity/identity from its current allocation and prove completion invariants.

checks.question: Is the conserved business fact/measure named separately from the allocation dimension being changed (box/container/series/project/warehouse/other analytic)?
Does the operation mutate allocation ownership without accidentally changing the total fact unless the business operation explicitly adds/removes fact?
Is a conservation invariant explicit (for example Σ fact before = Σ fact after) with identity/quantity normalization defined?
If an intermediate UNASSIGNED/unallocated state is allowed, are its owner, lifetime and permitted next transitions explicit?
Does completion block when required fact remains unallocated, duplicated or over-allocated?
Are repeated move/re-entry/retry operations idempotent with respect to total fact and allocation identity?
Runtime acceptance proves conservation across move A→B, temporary unassignment when allowed, repeated move and final completion.
Can reassigning an existing fact between analytics/containers increase or decrease total fact even though the business action only changes allocation?
Can a document/process complete while conserved fact remains in a temporary unassigned state that the business contract requires to be fully allocated?

learning_contract.definition_of_done: Every substantive task completes a knowledge-extraction disposition. A reusable lesson is integrated only when it can be routed, reviewed, regression-tested and blocks unsupported release.
learning_contract.project_specific_data_policy: Project/customer names, prefixes and one-off business facts remain task context or on-demand archive, not universal rules.
learning_contract.requirements_learning: Requirements discoveries are promoted as reusable rules only when they generalize beyond one project and have activation/enforcement coverage; project-only business facts remain project context.
learning_contract.promotion_evidence_policy: Real chat/model behavior may create a candidate lesson or LLM threat, but chat-derived technical/platform/vendor/standards claims remain discovery hypotheses until validated by reproduced target/runtime evidence and/or a current authoritative source. Supporting references may discover/challenge claims but do not become normative by agreement alone.

requirements_status_model.rule: Blocking OPEN/ASSUMED business decisions stop technical-ready status. Non-blocking explicit assumptions may proceed only as REQUIREMENTS_READY_WITH_ASSUMPTIONS.

requirements_contract_fields.title: Reproducible acceptance cases and correctness oracle
Business invariants / accepted and rejected cases
Smallest stable business identity and representation separation
Errors, absence, duplicates and alternative scenarios
Data lifecycle: source, transform, store, transmit, consume, change
Final observable state in every participating system
Authorization/access/rights conditions relevant to functional correctness

requirements_rules.title: Requirements traceability
requirements_rules.description: Prove need → target outcome → behavior/rules → implementation obligation → acceptance without substituting a technical action for the need.

checks.question: State the real need/problem and keep it distinct from implementation verbs such as add/automate/implement.
State an observable target business/system outcome and the target behavior that closes the need.
Trace each significant business rule/behavior to the need and to at least one acceptance case.
Resolve contradictions across task text, tables, screenshots, code/metadata facts and prior project constraints before design.
Do not demand internal code/module/query detail for an unchanged standard mechanism when its externally relevant behavior is already unambiguous.

When one requirement spans different artifact/mechanism obligations (for example metadata/subsystem membership, UI placement, form data binding and persistence), are they kept as separate traceable obligations with their own owning artifact/mechanism and acceptance evidence rather than collapsed into one generic “implemented” status?
Could two competent implementers produce materially different behavior because need/outcome/rules/acceptance are not traceable?

After mining available task/source/project evidence, are user questions limited to unresolved gaps that can materially change behavior, ownership, scope or acceptance rather than a generic questionnaire?
Can deleting an unresolved risk-required functional-contract field make the requirements gate pass instead of reporting the field as missing?

requirements_rules.title: Acceptance oracle
requirements_rules.description: Acceptance must prove both that behavior ran and that the resulting data/state/calculation is correct.

checks.question: Acceptance contains preconditions/test data and reproducible user/system actions.
Each significant action has an observable expected result rather than “works correctly”.
Correctness has an independent oracle: control values, expected state/data, cross-system payload/result or another reproducible proof.
Boundary/negative cases cover the business invariant where materially different behavior is possible.
Could the implementation pass the described steps while still returning a wrong business result?

requirements_rules.title: Requirements artifact claim provenance and readiness integrity
requirements_rules.description: Keep material requirements claims provenance-aware, prevent proposals/open material decisions from becoming agreed behavior, revalidate dependent claims after corrections, and adversarially test non-trivial requirements artifacts before calling them ready.

checks.question: For requirements-artifact work, does every material behavior/ownership/scope/acceptance statement preserve whether it is USER_CONFIRMED, SOURCE_OBSERVED, TYPICAL_RELEASE_PROVEN, DERIVED_WITH_EVIDENCE, PROPOSED_SOLUTION or OPEN?
Are model/analyst-proposed UI, metadata, data-model and technical choices kept as PROPOSED_SOLUTION until separately confirmed instead of being rewritten as mandatory requirements?

Is every unresolved decision that can change quantity, money, tax, identity, cardinality, match key, source of truth, rights, state transition, external/irreversible side effect or compliance kept blocking until resolved or explicitly accepted under the residual-risk contract?

When behavior depends on matching related rows/objects, is the exact match key plus 0/1/N behavior defined instead of vague phrases such as “other available analytics”, “available fields” or first-found selection?

After a material requirement correction, are all dependent claims/field mappings/restrictions/acceptance conclusions explicitly invalidated or revalidated instead of preserving conclusions derived from the old statement?
Before a non-trivial requirements artifact is declared ready, was at least one concrete counterexample attempted against the functional contract itself and dispositioned with evidence?
Is the requirements artifact kept BLOCKED/not-ready while any blocking OPEN, unresolved provenance, proposal laundering, correction fallout or required adversarial case remains?

requirements_rules.title: Process / role / state contract
requirements_rules.description: Stateful behavior must expose initiator, roles/rights, sequence, states/transitions and repeat/concurrency semantics.

checks.question: Identify initiator/actors and the actions/rights each actor actually has.
State trigger/preconditions, relevant before/after states and system/user transition sequence.
State repeat/re-entry behavior and whether a second user/process may act concurrently.
Can the same input follow materially different state transitions because actor/trigger/state ownership is unspecified?

If an eligibility/permission/classification/price/routing decision depends on mutable context, list its dependencies and state exactly when prior results are invalidated or revalidated after context changes.

requirements_rules.title: Data lifecycle / source of truth
requirements_rules.description: For changed business data prove source, meaning, owner, identity/representation, transforms, storage/use and repeat/conflict ownership.

checks.question: For every significant datum identify source, semantic meaning, authoritative owner and whether it is plan/fact/derived/representation.
Trace transformation, storage/transmission and final consumption; name the source of truth when duplicates/conflicts exist.
State behavior when source data changes or the operation is repeated/replayed.
Separate stable business identity from packaging/unit/barcode/display/normalization fields unless domain evidence proves otherwise.
Can two copies/representations disagree without a defined authoritative owner or conflict rule?

When significant reference/master data is replicated or cached, state authoritative ownership, semantic validity, freshness/version and propagation to every consumer; a technically valid stale copy is not sufficient source-of-truth evidence.

For composite target rows/objects, define authoritative source and calculation owner per material field; do not assume one upstream document owns quantity, identity, commercial conditions and derived totals simultaneously.

For a target row/object assembled from multiple related sources, are the target grain/stable identity, complete cross-source match tuple, allowed 0/1/N behavior and conservation/aggregation rule for material additive measures defined before implementation?

For each material field/source whose value can vary over time or lifecycle state, are the required effective moment/version, freshness tolerance and cross-source temporal consistency rule defined before implementation?

For every material quantity/amount/weight/price/other numeric fact, are its business measure, canonical unit/currency/scale, conversion coefficient direction, sign convention, precision and rounding stage defined before implementation?

For each material field/relation that may be missing, is the meaning of absence defined separately from explicit zero/false/empty/default values, including whether and where fallback substitution is allowed?

Is the required source-fact population/coverage defined at the business grain, including which facts must survive into the target, which may be excluded and the acceptance invariant proving there are no silent omissions?

When requirements move already-recorded fact between analytics/containers, identify the conserved fact, allowed temporary unassigned state and completion invariant so reallocation is not mistaken for creation/deletion.

requirements_rules.title: Integration functional contract
requirements_rules.description: A named API/method/message is not a requirement by itself; prove trigger → input → call → output → validation/transform → use → retry/errors → final state → acceptance.

checks.question: State trigger, input source, input semantics and mapping into the selected method/message/API.
State response/output semantics, validation/transforms and exact persisted/consumed use.
Cover authorization, pagination/async/timeouts when material; retry, idempotency, partial failure and re-entry semantics are explicit.
State final observable state in every participating system and acceptance that proves data correctness, not only transport success.
Is only an endpoint/method/field list specified while the functional chain before/after the call remains ambiguous?

requirements_rules.title: Analogy is not a requirement
requirements_rules.description: “Like X / by analogy” is only a reference. Explicitly state input, transferable behavior, output, differences/adaptations and availability of required source data.

checks.question: Name exactly what is reused from the analogy: input, rule/algorithm, UI, output/result, data contract or error behavior.
State differences/adaptations and prove the current source actually provides the data/conditions the analogy relies on.
Would removing the referenced analogy make the requested behavior impossible to reconstruct?

requirements_rules.title: Alternative scenario coverage
requirements_rules.description: Cover only materially different alternative paths: no data, duplicates, source change, invalid state/rights, retry, partial failure, concurrency and later overwrite.

checks.question: State behavior for absent/invalid data, duplicates and source changes when they can alter the result.
State error/retry/re-entry/partial completion semantics and idempotency where relevant.
State rights/concurrency and later lifecycle overwrite paths where relevant rather than enumerating theoretical exceptions.
Is there a realistic materially different path that changes result/ownership but has no specified outcome?

When the requirement includes forward and reverse/refund/cancel flows, does each pipeline have its own trigger, data/identity trace, state transitions and acceptance oracle instead of assuming reverse behavior by analogy from the forward path?

requirements_rules.title: Scope / assumptions contract
requirements_rules.description: Make algorithm-affecting scope, versions/contours, dependencies, assumptions and responsibilities explicit; unknown business decisions may not become silent technical assumptions.

checks.question: State what is in scope and materially relevant exclusions/out-of-scope behavior.
State version/contour/external-system/NSI/equipment/access dependencies when they can change implementation or acceptance.
Every assumption has impact and validation plan; assumptions that decide business behavior remain blocking OPEN questions.
Has an unknown business rule been converted into a technical assumption without explicit owner/impact/validation?

When implementation/capability depends on product/vendor release, is the exact target version/contour and unsupported boundary explicit, and are newer-version examples kept as discovery evidence until target behavior is proven?

When reproducing behavior from a legacy/previous system or release, classify each material behavior as REQUIRED_AS_IS, INTENTIONAL_CHANGE, KNOWN_LIMITATION_ACCEPTED or UNKNOWN instead of treating AS-IS behavior as automatic TO-BE requirement.

For every consciously accepted limitation/residual risk, record trigger condition, consequence, acceptance owner, effect on acceptance criteria and whether the new change must preserve, mitigate or leave it explicitly unresolved.

adversarial_case_contract.principle: A non-trivial adversarial gate is not closed by a generic review label; record at least one concrete counterexample/failure attempt and its disposition.

requirements_claim_contract.rule: A material statement must preserve provenance. PROPOSED_SOLUTION is never an agreed requirement by wording alone; hard-materiality OPEN decisions stay blocking.

legacy_compatibility.rule: Rules without proof_policy retain the pre-Phase-1 admissibility contract. This compatibility is explicit and executable; it must not be used for rules classified ARCHITECTURE_SEMANTIC.

independent_review.rule: Content/session separation reduces correlated self-review risk but is not cryptographic or externally verified independence without a separately trusted adapter.
